projects.title: Secure Document Link Gateway
projects.summary: Time-limited, encrypted links to documents stored on a remote system.
projects.problem: Users and business applications need access to documents that stay on a remote system, for a limited time, without the gateway keeping per-request state.
projects.architecture: A link service issues AES-GCM encrypted links. Each link carries its own expiry and the original URL. A background downloader fetches documents into a local store, a stateless gateway decrypts the link and streams the file, and scheduled jobs clean up expired documents.
challenges: Keeping the file cache consistent with link lifetimes across several schedulers, without per-request state.
decisions: Each link carries its own expiry and is AES-GCM encrypted, so the gateway can serve files without a database lookup.
Background jobs, not request handlers, fetch documents and remove expired files.
reliability: The expiry time is part of the encrypted link, so a link is refused after it expires even if cleanup has not run yet.

projects.title: XML Transformation Pipeline
projects.summary: Asynchronous XML routing and XSLT transformation with Java extension functions loaded from plugins.
projects.problem: Upstream systems send XML requests that must be routed and transformed before reaching their destinations, and failed messages must not be lost.
projects.architecture: Messages arrive on RabbitMQ and are routed to destination queues. XSLT stylesheets transform them. Stylesheets call Java extension functions from plugin jars, each loaded by its own classloader. Failed messages go to a separate error path.
challenges: Handling failed messages without losing them.
decisions: Each plugin jar gets its own classloader, so plugins can be replaced and the context reloaded without restarting the service.
Routing and transformation are separate steps, so each can change on its own.
reliability: Failed messages are kept and handled through a separate error path instead of being dropped.

projects.title: Messenger Archive & Semantic Search
projects.summary: A searchable archive of a personal messenger history, with voice messages transcribed and indexed, exposed to LLM agents through an MCP server.
projects.problem: A long personal messenger history is hard to search. Voice messages need to be searchable as text too.
projects.architecture: A Rust sync service pulls the history over MTProto into PostgreSQL. A Python worker claims transcription jobs with SKIP LOCKED and runs Whisper. A Rust indexer creates embeddings in batches and upserts them into Qdrant with deterministic UUIDv5 point IDs. An MCP server exposes search to LLM agents.
challenges: No transaction spans PostgreSQL, Qdrant and the checkpoint.
A long-running sync has to cope with rate limits (flood-wait) and retries.
decisions: Writes are idempotent: deterministic UUIDv5 point IDs, and the cursor is saved only after each upsert.
Transcription workers claim queue rows with SKIP LOCKED, so several workers can run in parallel.
reliability: After a failure, the sync resumes from the last saved cursor. Repeated upserts overwrite the same points, so they are harmless.
